summary: Checks whether a value is **not** a safe integer.
description: `nonSafeInteger(value)` is the same test as `!isSafeInteger(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.
An integer that an IEEE-754 double represents exactly. Beyond that range distinct mathematical integers collapse onto the same value and arithmetic quietly stops being exact.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is not a safe integer; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
nonSafeInteger(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER + 2); // => true
nonSafeInteger(1.5); // => true
nonSafeInteger("42"); // => true
nonSafeInteger(42); // => false
nonSafeInteger(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER); // => false
```
